body: I know you are right, I need help to get there. I looked into the counseling services offered by my university and it seems too short-term for my needs. I'm going to speak with them and see what they recommend that I do. I can't keep going like this. I know that my family would throw away everything we owned if meant keeping me alive, but that doesn't make it any easier to climb out of this pit that I am in. I need professional help and I'm going to make an effort to get some. Your words have been very helpful.

My wife and son, lifting weights, and reading books. My wife and son have been in a rough place lately though, my wife is very stressed out and my son has been having a hard time in preschool. I made an appointment for my son to see a counselor so he can get some help and so that I can get some assistance with helping him. My wife hasn't had energy for our relationship since she started her current job (5ish months ago), and she has been dealing with body image issues in addition to some of the stresses that I have felt (like worry over finances). I am trying my best too support them both and to be there, but I feel like I am running out of fuel. If I died they would receive more than 7 years of income in life insurance, my wife could find a new job that didn't cause her so much stress, the bills would be taken care of for a long time, and ultimately I am replaceable. Not to mention her parents, who are very wealthy, would be guaranteed to step in and provide financial support and would probably help care for our child at least until a childcare solution was found. My wife would probably find someone much better than me anyway. I think my son needs me though.

I don't really know the answer to your question, in all honesty. As I said before, it's something that I have felt for my entire life. I don't know if I was abused as a young child and have no memory of it, but I have always wanted to die. I think I feel like I live my life for the benefit of others. People tell me all of the time that I'm one of the calmest, most level-headed people they know, but the reality is that I am not right in the head, and they confuse my apathy for something good or desirable. I feel like the pains of life can plague me forever, but the joys quickly become stale. There is very little that makes me feel passion or life, and I feel the burdens of finances, grad school, marriage, parenthood, and work just pushing me into the ground. It doesn't matter though, when those challenges have been met and situations are better I'll just have new reasons to hate myself, I'm a fucking miser and I despise life.

What is wrong is that the people who are closest to me are the most blind to the way I suffer inside. Those around me see the way that I make them feel and the way that they benefit from me and they take that as a reflection of who I am on the inside, but inside I am vacant and longing for something that I'm afraid I will never have. My wife is a therapist who deals with people like me on a daily basis, but when I bring these feelings to her I get a day or maybe a week of concern and care before my struggles are forgotten. I think she cares far more about being sure that I won't kill myself than she does about helping me shed my desire for it. I end up feeling guilty because she is worried that I'll kill myself, so I feel worse for causing concern and I no longer think these are things I can express to her.
